You can use modals to talk about degrees of certainty and speculate about things in the past.
You use them to describe what is definite, probable, possible, or impossible from the speaker's point of view.

When you are almost 100 percent certain that something was possible, use must have or had to have.

must + perfect infinitive

We use must + perfect infinitive when we feel sure about something in the past.

When you are less certain, use may have, might have, or could have.

might/may/could + perfect infinitive

We use might, may or could with the perfect infinitive to say that we think something was possible but we aren't sure.

If Clauses With The Past Perfect tense
You use if clauses with the Past Perfect form to refer to time that is in the past.  The situation is not real, it did not happen. The facts are opposite.

You use this type of conditional to refer to an unreal past condition. If the if clause uses the Past Perfect tense and the main clause uses the Perfect Conditional.

Only the word "if" is used with the Past Unreal Conditional because you are discussing imaginary situations. "When" cannot be used.

Here are two structures:

[If ... Past Perfect ..., ... would have + past participle ... ]
and
[... would have + past participle ... if ... Past Perfect ...]
If I had known that winning a large sum of money would cause so many headaches, I would have hidden my excitement.
If I had recognized that, I would have made my answers more complicated.
If I had received such news, I would have been devastated.
someone who steals things from another person or place
Example: Thieves must have accessed my personal details.
These are words you hear between a customer and bank teller about identity theft.

images.text: Sally: Hello, I would like to speak with someone about opening a new bank account. I have recently been a victim of identity theft. Thieves must have accessed my personal details somehow and affected my finances. Here is the police report that details the nightmare I am living through. Bank Teller: Yes, Miss. Davis. Our branch manager has spoken to us. If I had received such news, I would have been devastated. Were the police able to apprehend the offenders?

Sally: They are still on the case. If I had known that winning a large sum of money would cause so many headaches, I would have hidden my excitement.
Bank Teller: I see… Did you keep the information to yourself?
Sally: No... not really. I must have told too many people about my luck... I feel so violated.
Bank Teller: That could have been the case.You currently hold two accounts with us, your credit card and a personal account.
Sally: I'd like to close the personal account and open another one with a different password. I'd like my monthly pay to be transferred to the new one.

Bank Teller: I think that's for the best. You will need to give your employer your new banking details.
Sally: I think I must have done that when I changed banks a couple years ago.
Bank Teller: While you are here you may want to change the password on your credit card and update your security questions. The suspects may have accessed that information as well.
Sally: If I had recognized that, I would have made my answers more complicated.
Bank Teller: A lot of people make that mistake. Repetitions or simple answers are not sufficient.
